headlines.title: U.S. oil rises above $100, Brent at five-month high as Iran says it's prepared for warfare
headlines.summary: WTI cracking $100 and Brent at a five-month high is the kind of tape that moves everything — airlines, refiners, EM currencies, and the long bond all reprice simultaneously. Houthi strikes on Saudi Aramco's Dhahran HQ plus Iran war-footing talk is a genuine supply-shock scare, not just noise. Energy names catch a bid while the rest of the market sweats the inflation read-through.

headlines.title: Meta hit with $25 billion fine for deceiving users on privacy
headlines.summary: A $25 billion jury verdict is not a rounding error — that's roughly two quarters of Meta's net income walking out the door, and it sets a precedent that puts every ad-tech and social platform on notice. META shares were already under pressure post-earnings; this piles on and drags the broader Nasdaq with it. Watch for contagion into Alphabet and Snap as the Street reprices regulatory tail risk across the sector.

headlines.title: France is getting its credit rating reviewed. The French debt turmoil has helped turn U.S. Treasury yields around. What comes next?
headlines.summary: Moody's reviewing France after-hours Friday is the kind of weekend risk that keeps portfolio managers awake — a downgrade could blow out OAT spreads and rattle the euro, with spillover into U.S. Treasuries that are already logging their biggest yield drop since the SVB crisis. This isn't 2012 redux yet, but sovereign stress in the eurozone's second-largest economy is a macro event that touches FX, rates, and risk appetite globally. The timing — right into a weekend with a Brazil election and Middle East escalation — makes it especially combustible.
